title: Game Builder Garage
subtitle: Build a game by connecting its parts
summary: Game Builder Garage is Nintendo's visual programming game, released for Nintendo Switch on 11 June 2021.
body: Game Builder Garage is Nintendo's visual programming game, released for Nintendo Switch on 11 June 2021. It introduces game-making through Nodon, characters that represent inputs, objects, logic and other functions. Connecting them creates working relationships: an analogue stick can move a person, a button can trigger an action and a condition can change what happens next. Guided lessons build complete small games before a free programming mode lets the player assemble an idea from the same components.

The connections make the cause of an action visible. A Stick Nodon reports movement from the controller, while an Object Nodon represents something in the game world. Linking the appropriate ports passes information between them. Testing the result shows whether that relationship behaves as intended. When it does not, the player can return to the programming view and adjust the connection or a value. The process turns an apparently simple action on screen into a set of parts that can be inspected and altered.

Seven interactive lessons introduce different kinds of games, while additional puzzles explain particular Nodon and their uses. The system can work with motion controls and other Switch inputs, and supports projects for several players. Creations can be shared through codes so that someone else can try them. The garage places learning inside the cycle of making and testing: a lesson supplies a useful pattern, and the next experiment asks what happens when the player changes the objects or relationships within it.
